title: Lineups of the Imperial, Superior and Eagle bands
summary: He recalls the members of the Imperial, Superior and Eagle bands as he first heard them.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: You remember a few people who was in the Golden, nothing, what was in that Golden Leaf is what I'm saying.

No, I couldn't recall who was in the, Maple Leaf. Only for Supreme Band and Maple Leaf Band, I couldn't recall. But I could give you the lineup of, like, the Eagle Band and the Superior Band, the Olympia Band and Imperial Band, those bands.
If you could run through that, do you remember? Yeah, I heard them.

Well, Imperial Band, when I heard them, they had that which was, Manny Paracis, was the lead of that band. And he had Buddy Johnson on trombone at that time. And he had Baby Matthews on drums. And he had George Buckhead on clarinet. And Willie Santiago on the guitar. And Jimmy Brown played the bass. That was Imperial Band. The Superior Band. The Superior Band. Now, pardon me. The Superior Band, in that band, I, when I first seen that band, they had, uh, uh, uh, Mac Murray on drums. They had, uh, Cock and Rumble right there. Eddie Atkins on trombone. Uh, Big Eye on clarinet. Uh, Bunk Johnson on, uh, Cornette. And they had, uh, uh, Rene Bautista, the guy with the cigar, always had a cigar on his mouth. And he was on the guitar. And, uh, Bill Moran was on bass. Bill Morero. He always said Bill Moran. Bill Morero on bass. Witches, Lawrence, whatever. And, uh, Simon and Jones. They were all family musicians. All strings. And, uh, I called Eagle Band, I think. I can remember that. Uh, when I heard them, they had, uh, had Oliver playing. Cornette. King Oliver. Joe Oliver. Joe Oliver. Had, uh, Bob Lyons on bass. Had Frankie Dusen. Um, Frank Dusen and Henry Zeno on drums. Frank Dusen on trombone. Bob Lyons on bass. Uh, Lorenzo, Lorenzo, Lorenzo Starr on, uh, on the guitar. And I'm trying to think of a clarinet player. I think his name was Warner. Not Warnick. Warner. Yeah. Yeah. Yeah. Yeah.
